COSP- WGG led Virtual Side Event- The Women Gaining Ground (WGG) organised a virtual side event at CoSP17 titled Reimagining Political Participation and Leadership of Women with Disabilities; Amplifying Women with Disabilities in Global South Movements for Feminist and Disability Right. This session took place in a critical year when over 80 countries held national elections but the , yet political participation of remained largely inaccessible for many persons with disabilities - —particularly women - —remained low; there were of course also amid global challenges such as climate change, conflict, and disrupted care systems. The panel addressed the systemic barriers to political engagement at the intersection of gender and disability, and the leadership of women with disabilities also within social justice movements. Despite progress, challenges persist, and the panel focused on exploring ways in which states and civil society can rethink and support in bold ways the leadership and political participation of women with disabilities. It focused on two regions - East Africa and South Asia, where women with disabilities are acting to have the political voice heard. Through the panel, the WGG consortium revisited the debate on political participation and rethink how both grassroot and international decision-making spaces can be designed to allow for thought leadership brought by women with disabilities. The panel was conducted in English with Bangla and Hindi translations, Indian, Kenyan and Rwandan Sign Language Interpretation, and CART available. Co-sponsoring an event co-hosted by the CRPD Committee and WEI- WGG organised a virtual side event at CoSP17 titled Reimagining Political Participation and Leadership of Women with Disabilities. This session took place in a critical year when over 80 countries held national elections but the political participation of many persons with disabilities - particularly women - remained low; there were of course also global challenges such as climate change, conflict, and disrupted care systems. In response, the discussion focused on structural barriers that continue to exclude women with disabilities from political processes at local, national, and global levels. Centering perspectives from East Africa and South Asia, the session explored how gender and disability intersect to reinforce marginalization, and emphasis the need for bold strategies to elevate the leadership of under-represented voices.A virtual training for WGG partners related to the CRPD- CRPD virtual training was postponed to 2025

No of messages/ dialogues for the 16 days of activism online campaign. For the 16 Days of Activism 2021, CREA led the digital consortium campaign from WGG on the theme of Your Protection Doesn’t Protect Me. Six activists and organizations took over CREA’s social media to amplify their own messages about why protectionist approaches to end GBV do not serve their realities, and the rights-affirming ways forward they want to see instead. The take-overs ranged from Twitter Chats and Spaces to Instagram reels and questions, often engaging directly with the audience and offering new perspectives to ongoing conversations. The “creators” taking over CREA’s social media were based in WGG’s priority working countries.
